actions.action: Check the soil and hold off watering until the top 2–3 inches are dry
Slide the plant out of the pot and inspect the roots
If roots are rotten, cut them back to healthy tissue with clean scissors
Repot into fresh chunky aroid mix with perlite or bark, in a pot with drainage holes
Alternatively, keep the nursery pot inside the decorative pot and empty any collected water
Remove dead and dying leaves at the base
Place the plant in bright, indirect light away from hot direct sun

reason: The answer correctly flags poor drainage and recommends repotting with drainage and brighter light, but its main diagnosis is overwatering and root rot, the opposite of the confirmed underwatering. Its 'stop watering' advice runs against the fix, though the soil-dryness check keeps it from being clearly harmful.
